Planning a Xilitla itinerary from scratch raises more questions than you'd expect: how much time to spend at the Surrealist Garden, which waterfalls to include and how to split up the days without missing any key stops? This Xilitla itinerary answers those questions with a tried-and-tested 3-day plan, organized around real opening hours and verified costs for 2026.

In this article you'll find a guide to what to do in 3 days in Xilitla: from the opening of Edward James's garden at 9:00 a.m. to the best restaurants to end your evening. Tours run daily departures from Ciudad Valles between 9:00 and 9:30 a.m., returning at about 8:30 p.m., which sets the natural pace of each day.

At huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and operators in the region. This guide is updated with real experiences from people who travel the Huasteca Potosina every week. If you want to start planning your trip before you finish reading, book your guided tour in the Huasteca Potosina.

Day by day: a Xilitla itinerary for 3 well-spent days

Day 1: Edward James's Las Pozas and downtown Xilitla

Day one of your Xilitla itinerary starts with a visit to Edward James's Las Pozas, open Wednesday through Monday from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., with last entry at 4:00 p.m.; it's closed on Tuesdays. The visit takes 2 to 3 hours. You can round out the afternoon exploring Xilitla's historic center and the municipal market, where local products like high-altitude coffee and piloncillo (unrefined cane sugar) are sold.

To end the day, check out the best restaurants in Xilitla to choose where to have dinner. Book a Xilitla itinerary tour with transportation included from Ciudad Valles.

Day 2: Sótano de las Huahuas and the mountain outdoors

Day two combines macaw watching at the Sótano de las Huahuas with hiking in the sierra. They aren't on the same tour of ours: Edward James's Las Pozas is on the Surrealist Route ($1,400 MXN per person), and the Sótano de las Huahuas, at sunset, is on the Tamul Expedition ($1,550 MXN per person). The recommended departure time is at dawn so you don't miss the birds flying out en masse.

After noon, free time in Xilitla lets you visit the nearby archaeological site.

Day 3: high-altitude coffee, markets and an easy trip back

Your last morning is ideal for visiting a coffee farm before noon. The farms offer short tours with a tasting included, a different way to wrap up the trip before heading back to Ciudad Valles.

Keep in mind that the road between Ciudad Valles and Xilitla can get tricky in the rainy season, from June to September. Seeing the available tours in the Huasteca Potosina helps you pick an option with transportation included if you'd rather not drive.

Our day tours priced per person range from $900 MXN to $1,950 MXN. If you'd like us to plan the trip for you, packages with a hotel in Xilitla, from 3 to 5 days, range from $8,699 MXN to $16,500 MXN per couple.

Tours run with shared arrivals daily through December 20, 2026, which gives you flexibility to choose your date. To understand all your expenses before you travel, see the guide on how much it costs to travel to the Huasteca Potosina.

Tips before visiting Xilitla and planning your route

Xilitla packs very different activities into a small area, but the logistics can fall apart if you don't plan for the weather, the season or opening hours. These tips come from the most common mistakes we see in travelers who arrive without a clear plan for what to do in 3 days.

  • Come in the dry season: October to February offers better access to hiking routes and less risk of closures due to rain. See the best time to visit the Huasteca Potosina.
  • Book lodging early: Places to stay near the waterfalls sell out on long weekends and holidays. See the options in lodging near the waterfalls to lock in a spot.
  • Plan your meals: Zacahuil (a giant Huastec tamale) and tamales de bola are must-tries; learn their story in the article on the history of zacahuil so you know what to order at each stop.
  • Essential gear: Bring light but waterproof clothing, shoes with good grip for the wet surfaces at Las Pozas and sunscreen. The humidity in the jungle is constant all year round.

Frequently asked questions about a Xilitla itinerary

How many days are enough to visit Xilitla and the surrounding area?

With 3 days you can cover the main attractions: Edward James's Las Pozas, the Sótano de las Huahuas and the coffee-growing area. If you also want to include archaeological sites like Tamtoc, it's worth extending your trip to 5 days; keep in mind that, for now, Tamtoc is open only on Sundays.

How much does a tour to Xilitla from Ciudad Valles cost?

The Surrealist Route, which visits Edward James's Las Pozas, costs $1,400 MXN per person with pickup from your lodging in Xilitla or Ciudad Valles (from Valles, $400 MXN extra per booking). The Sótano de las Huahuas is on the Tamul Expedition: $1,550 MXN per person.

How do you get from Ciudad Valles to Xilitla, and how long does it take?

Tours leave Ciudad Valles between 9:00 and 9:30 a.m., with transportation included from your hotel. The trip there takes about 2 hours on a mountain road. The return to Ciudad Valles is at around 8:30 p.m. In the rainy season, the drive can take longer.

Is Xilitla a safe destination for families with kids?

Yes. Edward James's Las Pozas and the main trails are family-friendly. For a plan of what to do in 3 days tailored to kids, see the guide to the Huasteca Potosina with kids. We recommend using a good itinerary planner to adjust the pace for the little ones.
